title: Mouse entered/exited signals don't fire when they should if the mouse didn't move
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.6dev3 ### System information macOS 15.0 ### Issue description When a Control node's visibility is toggled, behaviour of the entered/exited signals is inconsistent and counter-intuitive; - If your mouse is positioned over a control and it becomes `visible = false` the `exited` signal IS emitted - If your mouse is positioned over a control and it becomes `visible = true` the `entered` signal is NOT emitted The context in which this was discovered was that a control overlapping another would have its visibility enabled and the `mouse_exited` signal for the now hidden control underneath it would NOT get emitted until the user moved the mouse. This feels really janky and unexpected. In the screenshots below I put a black star to denote cursor position (with no movement) When the red panel becomes visible, I would have expected (blue panel exited signal and red panel entered signal): But the actual behaviour is (no signal emitted, current state is still that the blue panel was the last mouse entered event): ### Steps to reproduce 1. Launch MRP 2. Place mouse over the red panel 3. Note the behaviour of the entered/exited signal calls when the panel's visibility toggles on/off (and the mouse does _not_ move) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mouse-exit-signal-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23420600/mouse-exit-signal-test.zip)
